Her arms remained locked across her chest, her fingers digging into the leather of her own sleeves to keep herself from making another sudden, aggressive move toward him.

"Lost your wits along with your sense of purpose, then?" she asked, her voice dripping with sardonic venom. She leaned back against the crumbling masonry, her posture deceptively relaxed despite the tension radiating from her frame. "We are hunting Corvel. The man who's been bleeding this province dry for months, and you’re standing here playing the silent monk."

She tilted her head, a stray lock of hair falling over her brow as she leveled him with a piercing stare. "Remind me—who are we hunting?" she challenged, her tone dropping into a low, dangerous register. "Or has your memory grown as short as your temper? If you can't even keep the target in your head, you'll be dead before we reach the camp gates."
